units.title: Harbour Launch Slots
units.semantic_novelty_rationale: Orders five launch slots with both adjacency and a non-adjacency condition; the last slot is fixed. The first 20 questions are structurally equal as parsed JSON to the previously accepted 20-question v3 candidate; current practice and timed nearest matches show no semantic duplicate.

items.prompt: Five launches named Alder, Birch, Cedar, Dune and Elm leave at 09:00, 09:15, 09:30, 09:45 and 10:00, one per slot. Birch leaves immediately after Alder. Dune leaves after Birch but before Elm. Cedar leaves after Alder but not immediately after Birch. Elm leaves at 10:00. Which launch leaves at 09:30?
items.working_or_rationale: Elm is 10:00. Alder and Birch must occupy 09:00 and 09:15; if Alder were 09:15 there is no legal later slot for Cedar. Cedar cannot immediately follow Birch, so Cedar is 09:45 and Dune is 09:30.
items.provided_explanation: Elm is fifth. Dune must be before Elm and after consecutive Alder-Birch. If Alder-Birch occupied slots 1-2, Cedar must follow Alder but cannot be slot 3, so Cedar=4 and Dune=3. If they occupied slots 2-3, Cedar would need slot 4, leaving no slot for Dune before Elm. Therefore Dune is at 09:30.

nearest_matches.title: Exactly Two Heads in Three Tosses

items.prompt: At a fictional observatory, two independent alert channels operate on a given night. Channel A sends an alert with probability 0.30; channel B sends an alert with probability 0.20. What is the probability that exactly one channel sends an alert?
items.working_or_rationale: Exactly one alert is A only plus B only: 0.30(0.80)+0.70(0.20)=0.38.
items.provided_explanation: Exactly one means A alone or B alone: (0.30×0.80)+(0.70×0.20)=0.24+0.14=0.38.

units.title: Rehearsal Room Collision
units.semantic_novelty_rationale: Computes a birthday-style collision among three independent room choices via the complement that all rooms chosen are distinct. The first 20 questions are structurally equal as parsed JSON to the previously accepted 20-question v3 candidate; current practice and timed nearest matches show no semantic duplicate.

items.prompt: Three performers independently choose one of four rehearsal rooms. Each performer is equally likely to choose any room. What is the probability that at least two performers choose the same room?
items.working_or_rationale: Complement of three different rooms: 1-(4*3*2)/4^3=1-24/64=5/8.
items.provided_explanation: Use the complement. For all three performers to choose different rooms, the first can choose any room, the second must choose one of the other three, and the third one of the remaining two: (4/4)×(3/4)×(2/4)=3/8. Therefore the probability that at least two choose the same room is 1−3/8=5/8.

items.provided_explanation: Among rain-cover users there were 30+40=70 passengers, of whom 40 travelled in the evening. Conditional probability = 40/70=4/7.

units.semantic_novelty_rationale: Three-tag path derived from marginals and two pair overlaps with Music-Local forbidden; nearest current select-diagram items use full three-way overlap or disconnected four-set pairs.

items.prompt: A station has 39 programmes. A programme may carry the Music, Talk, or Local tag. Of these, 12 have Music, 18 have Talk, and 11 have Local. Four have both Music and Talk; three have both Talk and Local; none have both Music and Local. Five programmes have none of the three tags. Which diagram represents these data? items.working_or_rationale: Music/Local overlap is zero, so triple is zero. Exclusive Music=12-4=8, Talk=18-4-3=11, Local=11-3=8, with intersections 4 and 3 and outside 5: option A sums to 39. B omits required overlaps; C gives Music total 34; D gives Local total 8 and omits Talk/Local overlap. The encoded shapes/region keys require a separate render-topology check after blind commitment.
items.provided_explanation: Because Music and Local never overlap, no programme can have all three tags. Music-only is 12−4=8; Talk-only is 18−4−3=11; Local-only is 11−3=8. With five outside, diagram A matches every count and overlap.

units.title: Packaging Lab Fault Codes
units.semantic_novelty_rationale: Solves a 2:1 inside/outside equation in a four-set hub; nearest live hub questions select a diagram or identify one lettered intersection.

items.prompt: A packaging lab classifies samples by whether they need a retest and whether they have a seal, print, or weight fault. A sample can have at most one of the three named fault types. The diagram gives exclusive-region counts, except that the retest-only region is marked ?. The lab found that the number needing a retest is twice the number not needing one. How many samples are in the ? region?
items.working_or_rationale: Outside Retest is Seal-only 5 + Print-only 7 + Weight-only 6 + outside-all 3 =21. Retest total is twice that, 42. Listed Retest/fault intersections total 4+6+8=18, leaving ?=24. Named faults are mutually exclusive by stem; actual shape topology needs a separate check.
items.provided_explanation: Outside Retest there are 5+7+6+3=21 samples. Twice as many need a retest, so Retest contains 42. The three Retest-and-fault regions contain 4+6+8=18, leaving 42−18=24 in the retest-only region.
